records.subject: [PR #10744/23d3ee06 backport][3.11] Refactor WebSocket reader to avoid frequent realloc when frames are fragmented (#10747)

findings.message: @cython.locals defines data_len twice; the second declaration likely meant to be a different variable name (e.g., data_length). This can cause confusion or Cython compilation issues.

When assembling masked fragmented payloads, `payload_bytearray = bytearray()` followed by `payload_bytearray.join(self._payload_fragments)` is a no-op; `bytearray.join` returns a new object and does not modify in place. This results in `payload_bytearray` remaining empty and the payload being lost.

The old implementation preserved partial payload in `_frame_payload` and continued appending across calls. The new code stores fragments only in `_payload_fragments` and tracks length with `_frame_payload_len`. While `had_fragments` guards the reassembly path, any missed edge case could lead to lost or mis-ordered data; unit tests around multi-chunk masked and unmasked frames should be verified.

Removal of _check_sending_started() and associated request._response tracking means headers and body-related properties (content_length, content_type, charset, cookies, body) can now be mutated after headers have been sent, which breaks previous behavioral guarantees and may violate HTTP semantics or user expectations.

send_headers() no longer records the current response on the request object (request._response weakref removed). Any external or internal code relying on Request._response to inspect or guard against multiple/late modifications will now silently stop working.

Test removal (e.g., test_cannot_change_content_length_after_sending_headers and test_cannot_change_content_type_after_sending_headers) indicates an intentional change in contract, but there is no replacement coverage ensuring new intended behavior (e.g., allowing safe mutation post-send) is correct and consistent. This raises regression risk for existing users depending on the old constraints.

Only the first item from [options.extras_require] is used: cfg.items('options.extras_require')[0][1]. If multiple extras exist, their requirements will be silently ignored, which changes behavior vs the previous script that chained all extras.

Concatenating install_requires string with a single extras_require value (using '+') assumes both are newline-terminated text blocks. If formatting changes (e.g., missing trailing newline), the last install_requires entry and first extra may be joined on one line, breaking parsing.

requirements-txt-fixer hook now targets files matching 'requirements/.*\.in$' instead of excluding 'requirements/.*\.txt$'. This changes which files are processed and may be unintended if the tool is designed only for .txt files.

records.subject: [PR #9168/5e15ea61 backport][3.10] Avoid creating handler waiter until shutdown (#9210)

findings.message: Potential regression: previously shutdown waited on _handler_waiter only if it had been created; now it unconditionally creates a future whenever _request_in_progress is True, but that flag is only toggled in _handle_request(). If a request is in progress but _request_in_progress was not yet set (e.g., race around handler startup) shutdown may create a waiter that is never completed, or conversely may skip waiting if the flag was not updated correctly. This introduces subtle ordering/race considerations that are not obviously covered.

Behavioral change: _handler_waiter is no longer created for every request, only when shutdown() finds _request_in_progress True. Any other code that relied on _handler_waiter being non-None during request processing (even if currently there is none) would now see None, potentially breaking invariants.

Ordering / race risk: _request_in_progress is set to False before completing _handler_waiter, and _handler_waiter is only set if not None. If shutdown() has not yet created the future when the request completes, _handler_waiter remains None and no future is ever created or awaited. That matches the intent (no wait when no shutdown in progress) but any concurrent logic depending on the previous guarantee that _handler_waiter is always present and completed at end of a request may behave differently.

records.subject: Only check origin if insecure scheme and there are origins to treat as secure, in CookieJar.filter_cookies() (#7821)
Added a configuration flag for enable request task handler cancelling when client connection closing. (#7056)

findings.message: Removed handling of tulip.CancelledError and remapping it to tulip.TimeoutError. Any existing callers/tests that rely on cancellations being surfaced as TimeoutError (e.g., for uniform timeout handling) will now see a raw CancelledError or different behavior higher up the stack, potentially changing public API/semantics.

Removal of the assert on `self.writer is not None` eliminates an early, clear failure mode if `send_headers()` was not called or `writer` was not set. If other code paths can still leave `self.writer` as None here, this could convert a deterministic AssertionError into a more obscure AttributeError or silent misbehavior later. Verify invariants around `self.writer` initialization and uses after this point, or replace with explicit runtime check and error if needed.

records.subject: attach partial message to ServerDisconnectedError exception

findings.message: ServerDisconnectedError.__init__ stores 'message' but does not call super().__init__(...) or set args; this may break existing code relying on str(exc) or args, and is inconsistent with other ClientConnectionError subclasses.

New _started flag is only set in cb_on_message_begin and cleared in cb_on_message_complete; if feed_eof() is called after a low-level parser error or without a proper message-begin, _started state may be incorrect, potentially causing _on_headers_complete() to be called in an unexpected state.

feed_eof() now attempts to parse partial messages from _lines/_tail and returns parse_message(self._lines); parse_message may mutate internal state or raise in ways not reflected elsewhere. Swallowing all exceptions with a bare 'except' and returning None risks hiding real parsing bugs and makes behavior harder to reason about.

ResponseHandler.connection_lost now passes the return value of parser.feed_eof() into ServerDisconnectedError; for parsers that previously returned None, callers that expect ServerDisconnectedError.message to be unset or a string now receive a parser-specific object, which may be an API change.

records.subject: Add SSL related params to ClientSession.request (#2184)

findings.message: Behavioral change from using public headers mapping (`self.headers`) to internal `_headers`. If `StreamResponse.headers` adds validation, normalization, or copy-on-write semantics, writing directly to `_headers` could bypass that logic and cause subtle bugs (e.g., missing case-insensitive handling, lack of immutability after prepare, or future API changes).

Same concern for the CONTENT_TYPE presence check: `if hdrs.CONTENT_TYPE not in self._headers` assumes `_headers` behaves identically to the public `headers` interface for membership checks. If `headers` exposes a view with special behavior, this may diverge.

records.subject: Fix #1947: don't raise DeprecationWarning inside on_startup() handler for run_app()

findings.message: Grammar/wording issue in changelog entry: 'are not raise' is incorrect; should likely be 'do not raise'. Not a runtime bug but may need follow-up for clarity.

StaticRoute.handle() now returns HTTP 403 instead of HTTP 404 when accessing a directory with show_index=False (and 200 when True). This is an intentional behavior change but may be a breaking change for existing applications relying on 404 semantics for directory URLs.

Directory index generation uses self._directory.as_posix() length to slice paths (posix_dir_len). If the static directory path is a prefix of other paths in an unexpected way or contains symlinks, this string-slicing approach could behave unexpectedly; path-relative logic is slightly brittle though covered by some tests.

Method signature in documentation: `add_static(..., response_factory=StreamResponse \
                          show_index=False)` is missing a comma before show_index (between response_factory and show_index). This will render oddly and may confuse readers.

Changed HTTPRequestEntityTooLarge to require max_size and actual_size in __init__. If any existing code calls HTTPRequestEntityTooLarge() without arguments (or with a different signature) outside the paths updated in this diff, it will now raise TypeError at construction time instead of behaving as before. This is an API behavior change that may impact external users.

Introducing __slots__ without including all instance attributes will raise AttributeError on assignment. Verify that only _key, _connector, _loop, _protocol, _callbacks, and _source_traceback are ever set on Connection instances (including in mixins, tests, or monkeypatching).

Previously _source_traceback existed as a class attribute defaulting to None; now it is only an instance attribute. Any code relying on the class attribute (e.g. Connection._source_traceback) or attribute lookup on the class may behave differently.

records.subject: [PR #10422/289259d1 backport][3.12] Add human readable error messages for WebSocket PING/PONG timeouts (#10432)
Avoid calling the drain helper in `WebSocketWriter` if the protocol is not paused (#9796)

findings.message: Behavioral change looks inverted relative to the comment and typical flow-control patterns: previously drain_helper() was always awaited when _output_size exceeded _limit; now it is only awaited when protocol._paused is True. The comment states this is meant to throttle the WebSocket connection when the writer is not paused, but the new condition calls drain_helper only when paused, which may disable backpressure in the normal (unpaused) case and cause uncontrolled buffer growth or regressions in flow control behavior.

Type cast `cast(ResponseHandler, proto)` was removed. If `proto` can be `None` or another protocol type at runtime, callers relying on it being a `ResponseHandler` may now see type-checking regressions or, less likely, behavioral issues if incorrect assumptions were masked. Verify that `proto` is always a `ResponseHandler` here or keep the cast for type safety.

The input loop now uses `asyncio.to_thread(sys.stdin.readline)` which is blocking and line-oriented. Previously, `loop.add_reader` handled EOF by stopping the loop. New behavior cancels `dispatch_task` and lets `asyncio.run` exit. Behavior on EOF / Ctrl+D is intentionally changed; ensure this is acceptable for all platforms (notably Windows vs. POSIX) and that `sys.stdin.readline` semantics match the original `sys.stdin.buffer.readline().decode('utf-8')` regarding encoding and binary data.

After stdin EOF, `dispatch_task` is cancelled even if the server is still sending messages; this may prematurely stop receiving messages. Previously, the loop would keep running until explicitly stopped (e.g., via SIGINT). Confirm that exiting on stdin EOF is the desired behavior for this example client.

Changed `self._resolver.close()` to `await self._resolver.close()`. If `_resolver.close` is not always an async method or if existing code elsewhere expects `close()` to be fire-and-forget, this could raise at runtime. Confirm that `_resolver` is an `AbstractResolver` implementation with an async `close` and that it was previously a bug not to await it.

CI Python version bumped from 3.8 to 3.9. If the project still claims to support 3.8 or uses version-specific behavior, tests may no longer cover 3.8 compatibility. Consider keeping a matrix including 3.8 if support is intended.

StreamWriter.write is now async; all callers that previously treated it as sync must be updated or they will get an un-awaited coroutine. The diff updates main internal uses and tests, but any external or less-visible internal callers may regress.

Early-return paths (compression produced no data, or length trimming to empty) now return None from an async function instead of helpers.noop() (a pre-resolved future). This is semantically fine for 'await writer.write(...)' but may break any code that relied on the concrete Future object previously returned.

records.subject: Repr of old task class now shows "v2 compatible"

findings.message: TaskType.__repr__ now assumes every Task subclass has attribute __v2_compat__. This is safe for Task subclasses using celery.app.task.Task or celery.task.base.Task, but may raise AttributeError for third-party or legacy Task-like classes that use TaskType as metaclass without defining __v2_compat__.

Behavioral change: previously checked `'fanout' in c.conninfo.transport.implements.exchange_type`; now uses `c.conninfo.supports_exchange_type('fanout')`. This is likely a refactor to a helper, but may differ if `supports_exchange_type` implements additional logic (e.g., alias handling, feature flags, or raises on missing attributes) or if `implements.exchange_type` was not the only criterion before. Verify that `supports_exchange_type` is available on all conninfo implementations used here and that it is strictly equivalent (or intended) to the prior membership test.

records.subject: add task_received, task_rejected and task_unknown to signals module objects

findings.message: Changing @task(ignore_result=True) to @task means results will now be stored for this example task, which may be intentional but alters behavior and could increase backend load if many URLs are fetched concurrently.
Function semantics changed from returning a (url, status/int) tuple to returning only the length of the response body. Any existing code or tests relying on the previous tuple format will break.

In the exception handler, 'body' is never set, but the function unconditionally returns len(body) after the try/except. If an exception is raised, this will cause an UnboundLocalError. Probably need an early return in the except block or initialization of 'body' before the try.

README example shows urlopen.delay(...).get() returning '9980' (response size), which conflicts with the previous behavior (tuple of (url, 0/1)). If other docs or examples elsewhere still assume the old return type there will be inconsistency.

Logging format changed from %r queue (string) to %s with `q` (Queue object). This alters log output semantics and may not be intended; also inconsistent with `cancel_task_queue` which still takes `queue` string.
`q` is not defined in `cancel_task_queue`; this will raise a NameError at runtime when the method is called. Probably intended to log `queue` instead.

records.subject: Pidbox now always sets accept encoding to json only.  Closes #1870

findings.message: Mailbox accept types were changed from app.conf.CELERY_ACCEPT_CONTENT to a hard-coded ['json']. This may silently break deployments that previously relied on other content types (e.g., pickle, yaml, or custom serializers) for control messages, causing control commands or inspection to fail under non-JSON configurations.

Assigning consumer.on_decode_error = c.on_decode_error assumes that the Consumer instance exposes an on_decode_error attribute and that the consumer callback signature matches c.on_decode_error expectations. In environments where the underlying Consumer implementation differs, this could raise AttributeError at runtime or mis-handle decode errors.

Removal of explicit gc.collect() after cancelling timer references may increase memory usage or delay reclamation on platforms where cyclic garbage collection is not promptly triggered. Behavior change is intentional but could regress memory characteristics in long‑running workers under heavy scheduling load.

Timer._timer_count is set to count(1).next, which is Python 2–specific. If this code is (or becomes) run under Python 3, itertools.count objects no longer have a .next attribute, causing an AttributeError at import time. Consider using count(1).__next__ or a small wrapper function instead.

records.subject: Soft time limit error showed Trues instead of the timeout in seconds

findings.message: Inconsistent variable use: the warning message for soft time limit previously used `soft` (the soft-limit value) and now uses `timeout`. If `timeout` can differ from `soft` (e.g., represents overall timeout or hard limit), the log message may become misleading or incorrect while the exception still uses `soft`. Confirm that `timeout` is the intended value here, or this is likely a bug.

records.subject: Allow heartbeats to be sent in tests (#6632)

findings.message: Changing `without_heartbeat` from a hardcoded True to `kwargs.pop("without_heartbeat", True)` alters behavior only if callers already pass this kwarg. That seems intentional, but note that the parameter is now removed from `kwargs` before being forwarded, which is correct assuming the underlying consumer does not expect it twice. No clear defect, but worth confirming that no other layer expects `without_heartbeat` inside `**kwargs` and that tests cover both default and overridden behavior.

TokenBucket class is removed and replaced by kombu.utils.limits.TokenBucket. Verify that the kombu implementation has compatible constructor signature (fill_rate, capacity) and method names/semantics (can_consume, expected_time, internal time units) to avoid subtle behavior changes.

TokenBucket import switched to kombu.utils.limits.TokenBucket. Ensure the kombu version does not require additional initialization parameters and that its behavior matches expectations in snapshot rate limiting.

TokenBucket import changed to kombu.utils.limits.TokenBucket. Confirm that worker rate limiting logic still works correctly with the kombu implementation, especially regarding thread safety and token refill timing.

Removal of `App = Celery` compatibility alias may break external code that imports or references `celery.app.App` instead of `Celery`. This is a behavioral, backward-incompatible change for users relying on that alias.
Removal of `select_subset = select` compatibility alias can break external code that calls `Queues.select_subset(...)`. This is a backward-incompatible API change.
Removal of `select_remove = deselect` compatibility alias can break external code that calls `Queues.select_remove(...)`. This is a backward-incompatible API change.

records.subject: Improve celery command to use base.Command

findings.message: Command.usage signature changed from usage(self) to usage(self, command), but existing callers (e.g. BaseCommand.create_parser without command) may still call it with no argument, leading to TypeError unless all subclasses are updated.

prepare_args now assumes args is an iterable and unconditionally applies map(self.expanduser, args); callers such as CeleryCommand.handle_argv pass argv (a list of strings) as args, but parse_options previously returned (options, args) not (None, argv). The new use in CeleryCommand.handle_argv passes (None, argv) to prepare_args, which is consistent, but any other existing callers expecting parse_options semantics could now be broken.

Command now subclasses BaseCommand but does not set preload_options; previously BaseCommand.preload_options was prepended to Command.option_list. Now option_list omits these options, which may remove expected global options (e.g. app/broker related) from the `celery` command.

In Command.__init__, app_or_default(app) is removed in favor of super(Command, self).__init__(app=app). If BaseCommand.__init__ does not emulate app_or_default(app) behavior, code that expected a default app when app is None may now see a different app or None.

create_parser and get_options methods were removed from celery.bin.celery.Command in favor of BaseCommand.create_parser/get_options. Any specialized behavior (e.g., using plain OptionParser without preload options) is now different; could change CLI behavior or options set.

run_from_argv now uses prepare_args(*parser.parse_args(...)) which returns (options_dict, args), but colored flag is set via options['no_color']. This assumes the 'no_color' option key always exists; if missing, KeyError will occur. Previously it used options.no_color with a default from optparse.

Delegate.create_parser now delegates to super(...).create_parser then calls target.prepare_parser(parser). Previously target.get_options() were combined directly into this Command's options. If target.prepare_parser has different behavior or expects different parser construction, option/usage formatting may change subtly.

Adding top-level current_app.start() in __main__ means importing celery as a module via `python -m celery` entry semantics is fine, but if __main__ is imported in other contexts (tests, tooling), it will immediately start the app, which may be unintended. Also assumes current_app is fully configured at import time.

records.subject: Implements Inspect.conf command for getting worker configuration

findings.message: jsonify() raises ValueError for unsupported types. dump_conf now calls jsonify(dict(panel.app.conf)), so if any configuration value is a non-primitive, non-datetime object (e.g., classes, callables, custom types), this control command will raise and fail instead of returning data. Consider providing a safer fallback (e.g., str(obj)) or limiting/validating conf contents.

For tuples/lists, jsonify returns map(jsonify, obj). In Python 3 this would produce an iterator, not a list, which may not be JSON-serializable as intended. If this code is or will be run under Python 3, consider wrapping with list(map(...)).

jsonify() does not guard against recursive or self-referential structures (e.g., a list containing itself). Though unlikely in config, such structures would cause infinite recursion. If user-supplied data might be passed in, consider cycle detection.

Chord counter initialization changed from string '0' to integer 0. If any cache backend implementation or downstream code assumes a string type (e.g., string concatenation, lexicographical operations, or strict type checks), this may cause subtle bugs. Most numeric-increment cache backends accept integer initial values, so risk is low but worth verifying against all supported cache clients.

install_signal_handler now accepts either (signal_name, handler) or keyword mapping (e.g. SIGTERM=handler). This relies on string names matching attributes on the signal module when passed via **sigmap. Callers have been updated accordingly, but any external callers still using positional args with multiple signals or mixing positional and kwargs may misbehave. Public API change risk.

install_signal_handler uses sigmap.iteritems(), which is correct for Python 2, but will fail under Python 3. If this branch is ever run under Python 3, it will raise AttributeError. Confirm supported runtime.

reset_signal and ignore_signal functions are changed to accept *signal_names, and process_initializer now calls reset_signal(*WORKER_SIGRESET) and ignore_signal(*WORKER_SIGIGNORE). Behaviour should be equivalent, but any external code relying on the previous single-argument API plus list comprehension side effects (very unlikely) would change. Low risk.

Class attribute `_observers = []` is shared across all ChainMap instances. This means observers (callbacks) registered via `bind_to` on one app/conf instance will be invoked for all ChainMap instances, which is almost certainly unintended and can cause leaks and surprising cross-talk. It should likely be an instance attribute initialized in `__init__` or lazily.

`@router.setter` implementation `def router(self, value): return value` is a no-op and does not actually set `self._router` or any backing attribute. Calls like `self.router = self.Router()` in `_handle_conf_update` therefore have no effect and rely instead on `flush_routes()` side effects only. This is confusing design and likely a bug or incomplete implementation.

Subscribing `self._handle_conf_update` to `self.app._conf.bind_to` in `__init__` introduces a new implicit contract that `app._conf` is a ChainMap with a `bind_to` method. If any code constructs `AMQP` with a different config object (or before ChainMap gains this method), it will fail at init time.

New test method `update_conf_runtime_for_tasks_queues` is missing a `test_` prefix, so it will not be collected by pytest. This means the new behavior around dynamic `task_routes` updates is untested in the current suite.

The observer callbacks in `update()` are called with the same `*args, **kwargs` passed to `dict.update`. For configuration update notifications, callers may expect callbacks to receive a more structured or normalized representation (e.g., a dict of changes). This API is now locked in and may not match expectations; ensure all observers can handle arbitrary positional args.

Import path changed from `kombu.syn._detect_environment` to `kombu.utils.compat._detect_environment`. Verify that `_detect_environment` remains a public, stable symbol in `kombu.utils.compat` with identical behavior and importability across supported kombu versions; otherwise this may break on older or newer kombu releases.

Import path changed from `kombu.syn.detect_environment` to `kombu.utils.compat.detect_environment`. Confirm that `detect_environment` is available from `kombu.utils.compat` in the minimum supported kombu version and that `kombu.syn` is not still required for backward compatibility.

Same import-path change for `detect_environment`. Cross-check against kombu's public API and changelog to ensure this is the recommended, stable location and not an internal compatibility shim that may be removed in future kombu releases.

Bootstep.create assigns 'agent = c.app.conf.CELERYD_AGENT' but then calls self.instantiate with the string again instead of the local variable; if CELERYD_AGENT is not a valid import path this will fail. Probably should use the resolved 'agent' variable or validate config.

In state.stop_actor, 'ignore_errors(self.connection, consumer.cancel)' references 'consumer' which is not defined in this scope; should be 'actor.consumer' (or similar). This is a concrete NameError at runtime when stopping an actor.

Class is declared as 'class Agent(Actor):' but __init__ calls 'super(ActorManager, self).__init__', and contribute_to_state calls 'super(ActorsManager, self).contribute_to_state'. Both refer to non‑existent base classes, causing runtime errors. Likely leftover renaming from ActorsManager -> Agent.

state.stop_all calls 'self.actor.shutdown()', but Agent.shutdown is defined later; if 'actor' is not properly set on state instances, this can raise AttributeError. Ensure 'state.actor' is initialized and points to the Agent instance.

contribute_to_state sets 'state.connection_errors' and 'state.channel_errors' but the state class no longer defines maybe_conn_error; code in reset/stop_actor was refactored to use ignore_errors, but may leave dead/unused attributes. Verify that no other code depends on the old state API.
add_actor uses 'qualname(actor)' on what appears to be an instance; qualname typically expects a class or function. This may produce an unexpected name string and break remote instantiation.

Configuration key changed from CELERYD_ACTORS_MANAGER to CELERYD_AGENT. Existing deployments using the old setting will silently lose actor support or crash when Bootstep tries to instantiate a missing agent class.

Bootstep 'celery.worker.actors:Bootstep' is added unconditionally to Consumer’s bootsteps. If the Agent class or CELERYD_AGENT setting is misconfigured (or actors are meant to be optional), worker startup will now fail instead of simply not enabling actors.

Control.start_actor method has been removed, as well as the worker control panel handlers for start_actor/stop_actor. Any external code or tools depending on these control commands will break. This is a behavioral/API compatibility break.

Panel handlers start_actor/stop_actor were removed; coupled with removal of corresponding methods on Consumer and Control, this eliminates remote actor management functionality. If this is not an intentional deprecation, it is a regression.

New parameter `login_method` is documented as optional override but now bypasses the existing `either('BROKER_LOGIN_METHOD', ssl)` resolution logic; callers passing `login_method=None` may lose the previous env/config fallback behavior.

Use of `self.app.conf.BROKER_LOGIN_METHOD` inside `Celery.connection` is suspicious; within `Celery` methods `self.conf` is the conventional access. `self.app` may not exist or may be different from `self`, leading to AttributeError or incorrect configuration source.

New `failover_strategy` argument is threaded through to `amqp.Connection`, but defaulting to `conf.BROKER_FAILOVER_STRATEGY` depends on the underlying kombu `Connection` accepting this kwarg in all supported versions; if kombu is older, this will raise a TypeError at runtime.

Test assumes that when `BROKER_FAILOVER_STRATEGY` is `None`, `connection(...).failover_strategy` will be `itertools.cycle`. This constrains or changes kombu’s default behavior and may be brittle across kombu versions if the default changes or is not exposed as `itertools.cycle`.

Verify that all callers pass a name in the same form expected by pg_database.datname or that strip_quotes is known-safe here.

findings.message: Behavioral change in `convert_value`: previously converted values directly (e.g., returned float/int/Decimal), now returns a callable (converter function) or noop; existing callers that expect `convert_value` to return a value, not a function, will break.

Signature semantics changed from an instance method `convert_value(self, value, expression, connection)` to a `@cached_property` returning a function `(value, expression, connection) -> value`. Any subclasses overriding `convert_value` as a method will no longer be called as intended, and MRO/override patterns are disrupted.

`__getstate__` removes `convert_value` from pickled state, but `convert_value` is now a `cached_property`. On unpickling, the cache will be empty and recomputed, but interaction with older pickles or code expecting a method attribute may be inconsistent; comment references Python 3.4 only, suggesting legacy/partial behavior.

In `get_db_converters`, comparison `self.convert_value is self._convert_value_noop` relies on identity of the function object returned by the cached property; this is fragile and may fail if subclasses override `convert_value` or if the cached property is recomputed (e.g., after unpickling without cache).

Previous behavior converted falsy-but-not-None values (e.g., 0, Decimal('0')) according to field type; new lambdas still do that, but now `None` explicitly passes through. This matches the old early return, but any code that passed `None` expecting type conversion side effects (or error) will now get silent passthrough; worth double-checking against ORM expectations.

findings.message: Schemes are compared case-sensitively via membership in ['http', 'https']; while the tests only check require_https=True behavior, this preserves prior behavior where mixed-case schemes like 'Https' are rejected. Confirm this is intentional per security policy.

New logic treating scheme-less but netloc-bearing URLs (e.g. '//example.com/p') as 'http' is a behavior change: previously such URLs were considered safe when host matched and scheme was empty; now they are rejected when require_https=True. This appears intentional but may affect callers relying on earlier semantics.

findings.message: TupleLookupMixin.get_prep_lookup() now unconditionally enforces RHS to be a tuple or list via check_rhs_is_tuple_or_list(). If any existing code relied on passing other iterable types (e.g. QuerySet, generator, custom sequence) directly as rhs to tuple lookups, this will now raise ValueError and may be a backward-incompatible change.

get_lhs_str() treats lhs as iterable of fields when not a ColPairs instance. If lhs in some paths is not a ColPairs and not an iterable of objects with .name (or does not support len()), error reporting may itself raise an exception different from the intended ValueError. The new lookup compatibility branch assumes that the reverse accessor using default_related_name is present in opts.get_field(related_name). If related_name and default_related_name interact in unexpected ways (e.g., clashes or overridden related_name on a specific FK), this could raise FieldDoesNotExist at query construction instead of falling back to the legacy behavior. For example, a callable default returning an empty string or a value that serializes/deserializes to empty may now unexpectedly trigger `skip_default`, changing behavior for such fields.

The new early return for empty defaults on TEXT/BLOB applies regardless of `_supports_limited_data_type_defaults` and MySQL/MariaDB differences. This broadens the behavior surface and may unintentionally skip valid empty defaults on backends/versions that technically allow them.

The `_is_text_or_blob` helper relies solely on `db_type.lower().endswith(("blob", "text"))`. Custom field types or non-standard DB types that include "blob"/"text" as a suffix could be caught unintentionally, altering default-handling behavior for such fields.

records.subject: Fixed #28804 -- Fixed "Unknown system variable 'transaction_isolation'" on MariaDB.

findings.message: Assignments list now contains full `SET ...` statements but is later joined with '; ' and passed directly to `cursor.execute()`. This changes previous behavior of a single `SET a=1, b=2` into potentially multiple statements like `SET ...; SET ...`, which may not be supported or may be blocked depending on MySQL driver or server configuration (e.g., multi-statements disabled).

The isolation level setting changed from direct variable assignment (`tx_isolation`/`transaction_isolation` = 'repeatable-read') to `SET SESSION TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL <LEVEL>`. While more standard, this may behave differently on older MySQL/MariaDB versions that previously used `tx_isolation`, especially since `transaction_isolation_variable` was removed and no version-conditional handling remains.

The isolation level string is now uppercased only (spaces preserved), relying on `SET SESSION TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED` syntax. On older MySQL/MariaDB versions that return or expect dashed forms internally (`READ-COMMITTED`), there could be subtle compatibility issues compared to the former explicit dash replacement.

Test helper `get_isolation_level()` now issues `SHOW VARIABLES WHERE variable_name IN ('transaction_isolation', 'tx_isolation')` and assumes `cursor.fetchone()` returns exactly one row with isolation variable in the second column. If both variables are present (e.g., on some MariaDB/MySQL variants) this may return the wrong row or a non-deterministic one. Also, using `fetchone()` without ORDER BY can be brittle.

The test now normalizes the returned value with `.replace('-', ' ')`, but the production code no longer writes dashed values. Tests may no longer cover the different server representations of isolation levels as thoroughly, and may mask discrepancies between server values and what Django sets.

records.subject: Fixed #27032 -- Prevented setup_test_environment() from being called twice.

findings.message: The new test calls setup_test_environment() directly but never calls teardown_test_environment(), potentially leaving global Template state (_render overridden, _original_render set) modified for subsequent tests. This may cause order-dependent test failures or fragile coupling between tests.

Removal of Response.next()/anext() and NotRedirectResponse is an API-breaking change. If this project follows semver and this is not a major version bump, existing user code relying on these methods/exceptions will break at runtime (AttributeError / NameError) with no deprecation path.

call_next is no longer set when allow_redirects=False, and Response.next/anext have been removed. Any external code that previously used response.next()/anext() or response.call_next directly to manually iterate redirects will no longer work. This is intentional per diff but is a behavior change to document clearly.

Auth base class now exposes `auth_flow()` instead of `__call__()`. This is a breaking API change for any external custom Auth implementations still calling or overriding `__call__` instead of `auth_flow`, and is only partially documented in docs (which still mention `auth` being callable).

Docs list `auth` argument accepting "A callable, accepting a request and returning an authenticated request instance." but core now expects an `Auth` with `auth_flow()` and uses `auth.requires_request_body`. This may confuse users and is slightly inconsistent with the implementation.

Changed BaseClient to store headers via the property setter instead of directly assigning _headers. This now injects default headers (Accept, Accept-Encoding, Connection, User-Agent) at client construction time. Behavior change may surprise callers that previously relied on empty default headers or on Request auto-header behavior.

Headers setter now always starts from a fixed default header set and then updates with user-provided headers. There is no way to construct a client without these defaults except by manually deleting them after initialization; this is a semantic change and may not be fully covered by tests.

_merge_headers no longer returns the passed-in headers unchanged when both client and request headers are empty/None; it always returns a Headers object based on client headers. This is a minor behavioral change that might affect code relying on `None` or identity semantics.

Request.auto headers logic has been simplified to only add Host and Content-Length; defaults for User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Encoding, and Connection were removed. Existing users constructing bare httpx.Request without a Client will see different headers on the wire, which is a breaking behavior change even if intentional.

The new Host header logic only sets Host if `self.url.authority` is truthy. For URLs without authority (e.g. relative URLs or schemes without host), previous behavior may have differed; ensure this is consistent with supported URL patterns.

`extensions = dict(**extensions, timeout=timeout.as_dict())` assumes `extensions` is a `Mapping[str, Any]` with string keys; this will raise `TypeError` if a non-dict `Mapping` or a mapping with non-string keys is passed, whereas the previous `extensions["timeout"] = ...` only required `MutableMapping` semantics and accepted non-string keys.

Blindly rebuilding `extensions` via `dict(**extensions, timeout=...)` may drop entries for which keys are not valid `**` keyword argument names (e.g., containing spaces, starting with digits); previously such keys were preserved.

Changing `ResponseExtensions` from `Dict[str, Any]` to `Mapping[str, Any]` relaxes the type contract to allow non-mutable mappings, but calling code like `extensions["timeout"] = ...` (now replaced with a `dict(...)` copy) may still implicitly rely on mutability elsewhere; review other call sites using `RequestExtensions`/`ResponseExtensions` to ensure they do not mutate the mapping in place.

HTTPError.request is now a non-optional property that asserts `_request` is not None. Previous behavior allowed `request` to be None. Any existing code that instantiates HTTPError directly without a request/response, or accesses `.request` before the client populates `_request`, may now raise AssertionError, changing public API semantics.

Client now writes to `exc._request` instead of `exc.request`. This assumes all relevant HTTPError subclasses use the new internal `_request` attribute. Any third-party subclasses or earlier versions expecting `request` to be set (and not `_request`) may no longer behave correctly or may bypass the assertion in the new `request` property.

Removal of Request.read() async helper breaks any existing callers relying on this public/semipublic method for reading request content. Unless this method was private/undocumented or has a clear replacement used across the codebase, this is a likely backwards-incompatible change and may cause AttributeError at runtime.

records.subject: Make Origin use scheme, not is_ssl (#168)

findings.message: Origin previously keyed equality and hashing on `is_ssl` (bool) but now uses `scheme` (str). This changes behavior for any code relying on origins differing only by scheme representation (e.g. URLs with custom schemes that still set `is_ssl` True, or future protocol variants). Existing connection pooling or caching logic that expected http/https distinction via `is_ssl` may now behave differently.

Changing `__hash__` from `(is_ssl, host, port)` to `(scheme, host, port)` is a breaking change for use of `Origin` as a dict key or set element. Stored data keyed by Origin may no longer be retrievable if it was created under the old definition, and collisions/partitioning semantics change.

Docs now mention `.scheme` but there is no clarification of the relationship between `scheme` and `is_ssl`. This may confuse users about which to rely on and does not document the behavioral change in equality and hashing semantics.

findings.message: Wrapping __exit__ in map_httpcore_exceptions() may change or suppress exception types raised during context manager teardown, potentially altering previously documented behavior for users relying on specific exceptions from pool shutdown.

Using a synchronous context manager (map_httpcore_exceptions) around an async call to __aexit__ is unusual; verify that map_httpcore_exceptions does not rely on synchronous call semantics that could miss exceptions raised in the async teardown or behave differently under asyncio event loop scheduling.

Removed conditional dependency on 'async_generator' for Python < 3.7. If the library still supports Python 3.6 or earlier and relies on async_generator to provide async/await functionality or context managers, this may break those environments. If project has officially dropped support for <3.7 or no longer uses async_generator, this is safe; otherwise verify tests on 3.6.

findings.message: NETRC env var may be empty string; Path("").expanduser() results in current directory. This changes prior behavior where empty NETRC was skipped entirely and could cause an unintended attempt to parse ./ as a netrc file if it exists.

NetRCInfo.netrc_files now stores raw strings rather than Path objects; original get_netrc used Path and avoided invalid empty paths more explicitly. Behavior around invalid/custom NETRC paths may differ subtly from previous implementation.

Changing ResponseExtensions/RequestExtensions from Mapping[str, Any] to MutableMapping[str, Any] may be subtly incompatible with user code that previously passed immutable Mapping implementations (e.g. Mapping proxies or custom read-only mappings). While most real-world usages likely relied on dict-like mutability already, this tightens the expected contract and could surface as type-checker or runtime issues if code assumes immutability.

Ensure httpx’s usage of Extensions matches httpcore’s updated typing/runtime expectations; any mismatch in mutability assumptions between the two projects could lead to subtle integration bugs, though this change appears intended to keep them aligned.

records.subject: Wrap network errors in HTTPX-specific exceptions (#707)

findings.message: The new as_network_error context manager catches BaseException, which includes non-error conditions like GeneratorExit and KeyboardInterrupt. This may be broader than intended and could interfere with cancellation/termination semantics. Consider catching Exception instead unless there is a specific need to wrap BaseException subclasses.

Wrapping asyncio.wait_for/read/write/close in as_network_error(OSError) changes previously unwrapped OSError behavior into NetworkError. This is an intentional API change but may be backward-incompatible for users relying on raw OSError or specific subclasses (e.g. ConnectionResetError). Ensure this semantic change is documented and tested.

Similarly, wrapping trio.BrokenResourceError and OSError in as_network_error alters the exception surface area. Code that previously handled BrokenResourceError or OSError directly will now see NetworkError, which may break existing handlers. Confirm this aligns with the public exception contract and add tests for typical network failure scenarios.

ConnectionClosed now subclasses NetworkError instead of HTTPError directly. This is likely desired for hierarchy consistency, but it is a behavioral change that can affect isinstance checks and exception handling order in user code. Consider documenting this change in the changelog / migration notes.

Type annotation for `socket` in `set_open_connection` is `BaseSocketStream`, but it is called from `connect` with a `socket = await self.backend.open_tcp_stream(...)` assigned to `stream`. Ensure that the backend actually returns a `BaseSocketStream` or a compatible subtype; otherwise the type hint is misleading and may break type checking or subclasses.

`is_http2`, `is_closed`, and `is_connection_dropped` now assert that `open_connection` is not None. Previously, these properties were effectively unreachable before a connection was established; however, if any external caller accesses these properties on a fresh `HTTPConnection` (before `send`/`connect`), they will now get an AssertionError instead of a benign result. Confirm that such usage does not exist or adjust to handle `open_connection is None` more gracefully.

New abstract-like `OpenConnection` base class is introduced without being marked as ABC or enforcing interface beyond `NotImplementedError`. Existing `HTTP11Connection` and `HTTP2Connection` are updated to subclass it, but any external code that instantiated or type-checked against the concrete classes should be unaffected. Verify no external users relied on `HTTP11Connection`/`HTTP2Connection` not subclassing another base (e.g., for strict type checks).

findings.message: New broad try/except around body parsing will convert all parsing exceptions (including framework-specific ones) into a generic HTTPException 400 with fixed message, potentially hiding useful validation details and changing existing API behavior.

Wrapping `solve_dependencies` in a broad `except Exception` that always returns HTTP 400 changes previous behavior where internal errors (e.g., coding bugs in dependencies) would propagate as 500s; this can mask server-side defects and break existing error handling/monitoring expectations.

Use of `logging.error("Error solving dependencies", e)` likely logs the exception object as a separate argument instead of with traceback; typical usage is `logging.error("Error solving dependencies", exc_info=True)` or using `%s` formatting.

Change in response handling for `BaseModel` from `jsonable_encoder(raw_response)` to `serialize_response(field=response_field, response=raw_response)` can alter response schema/encoding; without corresponding test updates it risks subtle regressions in response formats.

findings.message: Behavior change: previously relied on np.logical_not(..., dtype=xnm_dtype) to produce float output; now performs boolean logical_not then astype(xnm_dtype). This should be equivalent for bool->float, but relies on xmask/concatenated mask being strictly boolean. If xmask or ymask could ever be non-bool arrays, this would change results (astype vs ufunc casting semantics). Worth confirming that getmaskarray always returns bool masks in these code paths.

For built-in dtypes ('float', 'int', 'complex', 'bool'), dtype is not a string, so calling dtype.startswith('complex') will raise AttributeError or TypeError. This will break benchmark setup for those params.

Using getattr(np, dtype) assumes dtype is always a string; however params also include built-in types (e.g. int, float). For those, getattr(np, dtype) is invalid and the code relies on catching AttributeError, but getattr(np, builtin_type) will raise TypeError instead in modern NumPy, so the fallback path will not be taken.

Expression self.data * self.data.T * 1j assumes .T exists and makes sense on a 1D array from np.ones(20000); .T is a view with same shape, so this works numerically but is a confusing / unnecessary transpose that may indicate a misunderstanding of array dimensionality.

Behavior change from `[...][0]` to `next(...)` only affects the exception type if no matching element exists. Previously this would raise IndexError, now it raises StopIteration. In this test helper, it may be assumed that a matching element always exists, so impact is likely minimal but worth confirming test expectations.

`return next(re.findall(dimpattern, v) for v in var['attrspec'])` changes failure mode when there is no match: previously `[...][0]` raised IndexError, now `next(...)` raises StopIteration. Also, the generator expression yields lists from `re.findall`; this is equivalent to the previous list comprehension indexing, so behavior is otherwise unchanged. Changing `list(sitepkgs.glob(...))[0]` to `next(iter(sitepkgs.glob(...)))` is fine when at least one match exists, but will now raise StopIteration instead of IndexError if no dist-info directory is found. findings.message: Removal of conditional inclusion of noprefix.h fully drops support for the legacy NPY_NO_PREFIX / noprefix.h alias API. Any downstream C extensions that relied on including numpy/arrayobject.h with NPY_NO_PREFIX defined (and thus expected the legacy unprefixed typedefs/macros) will now fail to compile. findings.message: Change from NPY_FINLINE to static NPY_INLINE alters linkage; if any code relies on these helpers having external linkage (e.g., by including generated header in multiple translation units), this could break linking. In practice they appear to be internal-only, so risk is low but worth confirming.

Removal of @name@_ctype_floor_divide for complex types is consistent with comment that it "should NOT exist", but if any out-of-tree consumers relied on it, this is a breaking change. Within NumPy it looks unused.

Float status barrier was moved from &out to &arg1. This should still enforce an ordered access pattern, but it changes exactly which object participates in the barrier; subtle FPE or optimization behavior could differ on some compilers/architectures.

Function pointer casts to (@otype* ) &out were removed and calls now use &out directly. This should be a no-op if @otype expands exactly to the declared type of out; if there is any mismatch in template expansion or typedefs, it could cause undefined behavior. Worth verifying the generated C for at least one complex and one real case.

Similarly to the earlier change, the float-status barrier was moved from &out to &arg1 in this code path. Behavior should be equivalent but could affect very subtle FPE/optimization interactions on specific compilers.
Dropping NPY_INLINE from @name@_float may reduce inlining and slightly affect performance; function semantics are unchanged, but this may be unintentional if inlining was relied on for hot paths.

Adding detection for __attribute__((optimize("O2"))) is benign if not used elsewhere. If later used inconsistently with global optimization flags, it could cause confusing performance or behavior differences, but current diff doesn’t show uses.

VERSION_PATTERN is not anchored, but Version._regex wraps it with ^\s* ... \s*$, so only full-string matches are accepted. This is intentional but differs from some uses of distutils.LooseVersion that tolerated surrounding text; verify callers never pass such strings.

Behavior change: previously warnings.simplefilter('error', ...) was enabled only when is_released(config) inferred a release build from _version.py; now it is enabled whenever numpy.version.release is true. Ensure numpy.version.release has equivalent semantics to the old heuristic for all build scenarios (e.g., dev, RC, nightly).

Cython minimum-version enforcement has been removed from this helper script (it now always calls `python -m cython`). This may allow too-old Cython when invoking tools/cythonize.py directly, diverging from setup.py and tests which still enforce >= 0.29.24. Confirm this is intentional or reintroduce a version check using numpy.compat._pep440.

Version comparison now uses PEP 440 parsing on the output of `gcc -dumpversion`. GCC version strings are not guaranteed to be PEP 440 compliant (e.g., '10', '10.3.0', or vendor suffixes), and invalid strings will raise InvalidVersion instead of being handled leniently by LooseVersion. Consider sanitizing/truncating the string or catching InvalidVersion to avoid breaking builds on some compilers.

Platform.release() values on Cygwin may not strictly follow PEP 440; _pep440.parse will raise InvalidVersion for unexpected formats, turning what was previously a best-effort LooseVersion comparison into a hard failure. This only affects tests but could cause spurious failures on some Cygwin kernels.

Switch from LooseVersion to strict PEP 440 parsing for Cython version. Non-PEP-440-compliant Cython version strings (e.g., distro-patched builds) will now raise InvalidVersion and error instead of being compared leniently, potentially causing unexpected test skips/errors.

Deprecation message uses gettext on a string with `{self.name!r}` but later calls `.format(self=self)`. After translation, `{self.name!r}` may not be preserved, leading to a literal `{self.name!r}` in output or a `KeyError`/`ValueError` from `.format`. Either keep an f-string around the translated template (using numbered/positional placeholders) or expose a format-safe placeholder like `{command}` and substitute that.

ClickException.show changed from f-string to `_("Error: {self.format_message()}").format(self=self)`. The translation string no longer contains a `{self}` placeholder, so `.format(self=self)` is a no-op. The literal `{self.format_message()}` will appear in messages, breaking error output. Use a real placeholder like `"Error: {message}"` and pass `message=self.format_message()`.

However, click.secho writes text plus a trailing newline by default (nl=True), so the expected bytes should likely be b'spam\n' unless other configuration strips it. This likely alters the call signature expectations for callbacks using this decorator and may break existing code relying on the old convention (where `obj` replaced the original first argument). Needs verification against Click’s documented behavior and existing call sites/tests.

Changing `prompt_text = t.cast(str, prompt)` to `prompt_text = prompt` removes a runtime cast that previously ensured `prompt_text` was a string. If callers passed non-string truthy values (e.g. integers or objects), behavior may change or break where a string is expected. Verify type of `prompt` is guaranteed to be `str` at runtime.

Removal of `confirmation_prompt = t.cast(str, confirmation_prompt)` relies on `confirmation_prompt` already being a string when truthy. If external callers or future code pass non-string truthy values, this could cause subtle UI or type issues. Likely OK but worth confirming type guarantees.

Variable `t` is replaced by `dt` and then `yield t.cast(str, dt)` is introduced. This appears to intend `typing.cast`, but `t` is now a shadowed name of the typing module variable used elsewhere, and mypy expects `typing.cast(str, dt)`. At runtime `t` here is a string (the path), so `t.cast` will raise `AttributeError`. This is a concrete defect and should be corrected to `yield typing.cast(str, dt)` or similar.

records.subject: Fix _pipepager()/_tempfilepage() to work with multi-call binaries

findings.message: Behavior change from Path.resolve() to Path.absolute(): symlinks are no longer resolved. This is intentional for multi-call binaries like busybox, but may alter behavior in environments relying on following symlinks (e.g., wrapper scripts or symlinks pointing to alternate pagers). Consider whether any supported platforms depend on the realpath of the pager binary.

ParameterSource changed from a string-valued helper class to an enum.Enum with auto() values; this is intentionally breaking for any external code that compares or serializes the old string constants or calls ParameterSource.validate. If such external usage exists, this may require a follow-up deprecation or compatibility shim.

Context attribute renamed from _source_by_paramname to _parameter_source. If any external code accessed the private _source_by_paramname attribute directly, this will break it. Public API (get_parameter_source / set_parameter_source) remains consistent.

Tests now assert on ctx.get_parameter_source returning an enum member instead of string equality, which aligns with the code change. However, this confirms the behavioral change; any user code expecting a string (e.g. printing or logging without .name) will observe different output.

Using `ctx.lookup_default(self.name) or self.default` will treat any falsey mapped default (e.g. 0, False, "") as if it were not present, falling back to the option's own default. This may be intended for empty env vars (as per changelog), but could be surprising for valid falsey default_map values. Consider explicitly checking for `is not None` instead of using `or` if falsey defaults should be allowed.

records.subject: Underscores are now replaced by dashes in commands

findings.message: Changing the implicit command name from f.__name__.lower() to f.__name__.lower().replace('_', '-') is a behavior change that may break existing CLIs that relied on underscores in auto-generated subcommand names or introspected ctx.info_name values.

The docstring now documents underscore-to-dash replacement, confirming this as an intentional public behavior change; nonetheless, there is migration risk for existing users who did not pass an explicit name and used underscores in command function names.

Existing tests (subcommand naming, environment variables, and variable precedence) were removed and replaced with new deprecation tests. This significantly reduces coverage of existing behavior and may hide regressions unrelated to the new feature.
New import `style` from `.termui` will raise ImportError if older or alternate termui implementations do not provide `style`. Confirm compatibility across supported environments.

_maybe_show_deprecated_notice assumes `cmd` has a `.deprecated` attribute. Although `Command` now defines it, any third-party/extended command-like objects passed here that don't define `.deprecated` will raise AttributeError. Consider using `getattr(cmd, 'deprecated', False)`.

Help text is modified in-place by appending `DEPRECATED_HELP_NOTICE` to `self.help`. If `self.help` is reused (e.g., same Command instance invoked multiple times or help formatter called multiple times), the marker may be appended repeatedly. Consider not mutating `self.help` and instead building a derived string.

_maybe_show_deprecated_notice is called unconditionally on `Command.invoke`. For multi-command hierarchies, ensure this doesn’t result in duplicate or unexpected warnings when higher-level invocations wrap child commands.
In `test_deprecated_in_invocation`, `deprecated_cmd` calls `debug()` which is not imported or defined in this file. This will cause a NameError during the test, failing the test suite.

records.subject: renamed context to environment to reduce confusion

findings.message: Renamed Context -> Environment and pass_context -> pass_environment. Any external code, tests, or documentation importing Context or pass_context from complex.cli will now break. Within this diff all internal references are updated, but cross-module usage outside this example should be checked.

Previous fallback behavior used `sys._getframe` and `pkg_resources` entry points to infer a version based on the calling module when `version=None`. That logic is removed; now only `importlib.metadata.version(prog)` or its backport is used, which may fail to find a version for existing setups that relied on entry point/module mapping.

The new logic calls `get_version(prog)` where `prog` is derived from the Click context (command name). This assumes the distribution name and command name match; in many real-world packages, console script names differ from the distribution name, so `importlib.metadata.version(prog)` can raise `PackageNotFoundError`, causing `RuntimeError('Could not determine version')` where the old implementation would have resolved a version via entry points.

No handling is added for `importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError` (or generic `Exception`) around `get_version(prog)`. For commands where the package metadata is not installed or the name mismatches, this will now raise and break `--version` unexpectedly, whereas previous behavior might have worked or failed more conservatively.

The tests requirements add `importlib_metadata` but not conditionally (e.g., only for Python < 3.8). This is probably harmless but may be unnecessary on newer Pythons; ensure CI matrix accounts for differing stdlib vs backport usage.

Behavior change: when args is None on Windows, sys.argv[1:] is now expanded via _expand_args (user, env, glob). This may surprise existing scripts that relied on literal patterns or raw env references. The docstring notes the change but downstream impact should be considered.

Expansion order is user -> env -> glob. This is reasonable, but differs from some shells (e.g., env expansion before ~ in some contexts). Not necessarily a bug, but behavior may not exactly match user expectations from Unix shells.

Type hints use typing.Iterable and List, but the rest of the codebase might not be consistently typed. This is low risk but could cause mild tooling inconsistencies only if type checking conventions differ.

Changing Jinja2 dependency to MarkupSafe for escape/Markup imports in src/flask/__init__.py requires that MarkupSafe be present at runtime via transitive dependencies. If a minimal environment installs Flask without Jinja2 (or with an older Jinja2 that doesn’t pull in a compatible MarkupSafe), imports may fail. Consider explicitly ensuring a suitable MarkupSafe version via dependencies or confirming transitive guarantees.

records.subject: Fix callback order for nested blueprints

findings.message: Changed template context processor resolution to build funcs via chaining from an empty iterable and to reverse request.blueprints. This is a behavioral change for nested blueprints; tests cover the intended order, but downstream code that relied on previous (arguably incorrect) order may see subtle behavior changes.

URL default functions for blueprints now iterate over reversed(bps). This intentionally changes resolution order; low risk of runtime defect but may cause behavior changes where multiple blueprints define defaults for the same endpoint segments.

before_request and url_value_preprocessors are now collected starting from an empty iterable, iterating chain([None], reversed(request.blueprints)). This fixes nested blueprint order but also slightly changes behavior when no functions are registered (no longer relying on indexing [None]); should be safe but worth ensuring self.before_request_funcs[None] is always present or None-key use is optional as assumed.

after_request_funcs and teardown_request_funcs iteration order for app vs blueprints has been adjusted (now blueprint names then None). This is a deliberate semantic change for ordering; tests were added for before/teardown and context processors but not explicitly for after_request, so an additional focused test on after_request ordering with nested blueprints would reduce risk.

records.subject: Updated a comment that was misleading with recent flask sqlalchemy installations
phased out shared data middleware in flask for send_file

findings.message: Static serving behavior changes from Werkzeug SharedDataMiddleware to a custom send_static_file view. This may alter handling of caching, range requests, directory indexes, or other edge cases compared to the previous middleware, potentially breaking existing expectations.

The static endpoint is no longer marked build_only=True. This exposes /static/<filename> as a routed view instead of relying solely on the middleware. While this is likely intentional, it changes behavior and may conflict with user-defined routes or assumptions about static being non-view-based.

posixpath.normpath + startswith('../') is used to prevent directory traversal, but it does not guard against absolute paths (e.g., '/etc/passwd' on POSIX) or backslash-based traversal on Windows. However, the rule uses <filename> with URL paths, so in practice it is probably safe; still, consider explicitly rejecting absolute paths for defense in depth.

send_static_file builds its own path with os.path.join(self.root_path, 'static', filename), ignoring pkg_resources-based package data used previously for static files. Apps that relied on package resource loading for static assets may see changed or broken static file resolution.

send_file now only prefixes current_app.root_path for non-absolute paths. This is a behavior change: code that previously passed an absolute path assuming it would be re-rooted under app.root_path will now use that absolute path directly. This is likely a bugfix/improvement but could break callers depending on the old behavior.

Passing subdomain=module.subdomain to add_url_rule for static files assumes that all modules define a .subdomain attribute and that it is a valid value for Flask's subdomain routing. If module.subdomain is missing or None/unexpected type, this can raise AttributeError or misconfigure routes at import/registration time.

This change alters the routing behavior for all module static file endpoints by constraining them to a subdomain. Existing code may rely on these static routes being available on the main/default domain; adding subdomain routing can break URL generation and static asset delivery for modules not intended to be subdomain-scoped.

Behavior change: previously returned value from update_wrapper(wrapper_func, f) was a Callable with functools.wraps-applied metadata; now it is the same object but with a typing-only cast. At runtime cast() is a no-op, so behavior is effectively unchanged. The only change is adding a more precise TypeVar bound and cast for type checking. This is very unlikely to introduce a runtime regression.

Change from inspecting loader.__module__/__name__ to loader.__class__.__module__/__class__.__name__ is likely correct for typical loader instances, but may alter behavior if a custom loader previously spoofed these attributes directly on the instance. This is a low‑risk compatibility concern more than a clear defect.

records.subject: Reduce unnecessary function calls. When propagate exceptions, the function call of "_find_error_handler" makes no sense.

findings.message: Behavioral change: _find_error_handler(InternalServerError()) is now called only after self.log_exception and only when propagate_exceptions is False. Previously it was called unconditionally before potential re-raising. This is probably an intended optimization/behavioral fix (avoiding handler lookup when exception is re-propagated), but it does slightly change timing/side-effects if custom error handlers or signals rely on the earlier call. Risk is low but worth being aware of in case handlers have side effects beyond producing a response.

records.subject: Added shebang to the test run file
Unify the uses of "file system" vs "fileystem".

findings.message: Return type annotation for template_test is incorrect: it declares `| T_template_filter` instead of `| T_template_test`. This doesn’t affect runtime but is a typing/API correctness issue.
Return type annotation for template_global is incorrect: it declares `| T_template_filter` instead of `| T_template_global`.
Return type annotation for app_template_test is incorrect: it declares `| T_template_filter` instead of `| T_template_test`.
Return type annotation for app_template_global is incorrect: it declares `| T_template_filter` instead of `| T_template_global`.

Behavior change: errorhandler decorator now calls public register_error_handler without passing key=None. Previously _register_error_handler(None, ...) forced app-level registration; now behavior depends on register_error_handler implementation (which may support blueprints or different routing). This can subtly change where handlers are registered.

Hard-coding self.error_handler_spec[None] removes previous flexibility for non-None keys (e.g., blueprint-specific handlers) that _register_error_handler may have been used for. Any existing callers using _register_error_handler with a non-None key will now incorrectly store handlers under the None key.

The _register_error_handler method is removed entirely. If any subclass, extension, or external code overrides or calls this protected method (common in Flask ecosystem), this is a breaking change and will cause AttributeError or lost custom behavior.

Behavior change on Python 2: previously attempted `str(value)` (using default encoding, often utf-8) and kept original on UnicodeError; now attempts `value.encode('ascii')`, which will raise UnicodeError for any non-ASCII character. This can cause previously valid, non-ASCII string interpolations to fail or behave differently.

The new branch only runs on PY2, but on Python 3 the old behavior was effectively a no-op due to 2to3. The change may be intended to narrow scope to Python 2 but alters encoding semantics without clear migration handling or tests shown here.

records.subject: Fixed a few spelling mistakes in a docstring

findings.message: TemplateNotFound is now raised with two arguments (name, message). This assumes TemplateNotFound.__init__ accepts both and preserves backward-compatible behavior for callers that depend on attributes like 'name', 'message', or args[0]. Verify that this signature matches the existing exception API across environments.

records.subject: Use a separate scope for the loop else branch

findings.message: Leftover debugging statement `print(else_frame.symbols.__dict__)` will emit to stdout during template compilation, changing behavior and polluting output/logs.

RootVisitor._simple_visit signature changed to accept **kwargs, but FrameSymbolVisitor.visit is still called without propagating **kwargs; for nodes where RootVisitor.visit_* now expects kwargs (e.g. visit_For with for_branch), this may cause inconsistent behavior if invoked via _simple_visit or future extensions.

visit_For now has a custom signature (for_branch, **kwargs); if other parts of the system call RootVisitor.visit(node) expecting the old behavior (full subtree including target, body, else), they will now only analyze the selected branch, which may regress symbol tracking in non-compiler callers.

records.subject: include tags are now able to select between multiple templates and take the first that exists, if a list of templates is given.

findings.message: Removal of the autoescape-based `Markup` wrapping logic in `TemplateReference.__getitem__` changes behavior for block access: previously, blocks retrieved via this path would be wrapped when autoescaping was enabled; now they are returned unwrapped. This is a silent behavioral change that may break templates relying on autoescaping of block content or parity with other block access paths. Confirm that this code is truly dead/unused or that equivalent wrapping occurs inside `BlockReference` before merging.

Variable `state` is no longer explicitly set to 'root' when the initial `state` argument is None. This relies on `stack = ['root']` and `stack[-1]` driving state indirectly. If any downstream code depends on `state` itself (e.g. for error messages or debugging), this silent change in value may be observable.

The new lstrip logic uses `next(g for g in groups[2::2] if g is not None)` and assumes there is always at least one non-None whitespace control group. If the regex match ever produces all-None values in these positions (for example, due to future changes to the lexer rules), this will raise `StopIteration` and break tokenization.

records.subject: parametrize tests argument order consistent with existing filters add changelog

findings.message: Docstring for do_max incorrectly says 'Return the smallest item from the sequence.' (copy-paste from min); should describe largest item, risk of user confusion but not runtime bug.
Docstring param description for `attribute` in do_min says 'Get the object with the max value of this attribute.' which is incorrect; it should refer to the min value when using min.

Docstring param description for `attribute` in do_max also says 'Get the object with the max value of this attribute.' but examples/tests show max is over `value` attribute already; wording is at least confusing and likely copy-paste error from do_min.

Change of _min_or_max signature/argument order is correct in current call sites, but this is a non-private helper in the module; if imported or used elsewhere out of tree, this is a silent breaking change (behavioral regression risk).

Error message for empty sequence in _min_or_max changed from 'sequence was empty' to 'sequence was empty.' (added period). If external tests or callers rely on exact undefined message text, this is a subtle backward incompatibility.

records.subject: map filter can use False as default

findings.message: Changing `if default and isinstance(item, Undefined):` to `if default is not None and isinstance(item, Undefined):` alters behavior for all callers relying on the previous truthiness check. Previously, only truthy defaults were applied; now any non-None default (including 0, '', [], False) will be used, which may be a backwards-incompatible behavior change for existing templates.

records.subject: Fixed loop.last to not consume the entire iterator to determine if this is the last iteration of the loop.

findings.message: Changing `last` from `index0 + 1 == length` to a lookahead-based `LoopContext.End` check alters semantics: for any iterable where `length` was previously known (e.g., sequences, ranges, generators with `__len__`), `last` is now computed solely by iterator exhaustion rather than the cached length. This can diverge from old behavior if the underlying iterable's length is non-standard, changes during iteration, or is inconsistent with iteration. This is an intentional behavior change but may be a subtle BC break.

Introducing `_after` with eager `_safe_next()` performs a lookahead read from the iterator at loop creation time. For side-effectful iterators, or iterables expected not to be consumed until the first iteration, this changes when side effects occur (earlier) compared to the pre-change behavior where `next` was only called during iteration.

The iteration logic now uses `_after` and `_safe_next()` and raises `StopIteration` when `_after` is `End`. Two potential risks: (1) if `LoopContext.End` is ever shadowed/compared incorrectly, the stop condition could misfire; (2) any external code that reuses or inspects `context._iterator` directly (outside normal Jinja2 contracts) will see it already advanced one step relative to index0, which may cause subtle bugs. These are low-probability but non-zero regression risks.

Package __version__ changed to '2.7.2-dev'. Verify this is intentional for a development/pre-release version and that any tooling expecting a final release version (e.g., strict semver checks) can handle the '-dev' suffix.
setup(version='2.7.2-dev') now matches __init__.__version__. Ensure any release or packaging automation supports non-final version strings with '-dev' suffix.

New code removes the broad try/except around CodeType construction. Previously, environments that disallowed code object modification (e.g., certain restricted runtimes) would fall back silently; now this will raise, potentially breaking existing users relying on that behavior.

For Python < 3.8 the manual CodeType constructor no longer attempts to account for version-specific arguments such as posonlyargcount or linetable. This is likely fine for 3.7 and below, but if any backported or non-CPython implementations expose different CodeType signatures, this may fail at runtime.

records.subject: Fixed a small bug with the undefined object: the error message on divisions with undefined objects was misleading.

findings.message: Behavior change: __div__ / __rdiv__ and __realdiv__ / __rrealdiv__ are removed from the alias chain and replaced with __truediv__ / __rtruediv__. In Python 2, removal of __div__ can change how Undefined interacts with the legacy division operator '/' versus '__truediv__'. This is likely intentional (modernization) but may break existing code that relied on old-style division behavior raising UndefinedError via those specific dunder methods.

New operators __pow__ and __rpow__ for Undefined now mapped to _fail_with_undefined_error. This is likely correct and consistent, but if any template previously relied on a different behavior (e.g., custom subclass overriding __pow__), behavior will change. Risk is low but non-zero.

Bug fix/change in attribute resolution: inside the AttributeError handler, dict-style access now uses key 'attribute' instead of 'argument'. This looks like a correctness fix (previously used an undefined/incorrect variable) but may alter behavior if callers relied on the old, arguably buggy, use of 'argument'. Verify that 'attribute' is the intended lookup key and that no external code depends on the previous behavior.

records.subject: Updated docs on autoescaping and made select_autoescape case insensitive
Add support back for custom resolves on old resolve method

findings.message: Context is converted from a plain class with __slots__ to a with_metaclass(ContextMeta) class and __slots__ are removed. This may increase memory usage and can break user code that relied on attribute restrictions or slot layout.

ContextMeta.__new__ references Context.resolve and Context.resolve_or_missing while Context is defined later in the file. Although Python resolves these as globals at call time and not at function definition, this tight self-reference in class creation logic is subtle and easy to regress if the class name or structure changes.

The fast-path optimization sets self.resolve_or_missing = resolve_or_missing in __init__. Any user subclass that overrides resolve_or_missing but is detected as _fast_resolve_mode will have its override silently bypassed, which may be a behavior change for some custom contexts.

In Context.resolve, when _legacy_resolve_mode is True, it calls the module-level resolve_or_missing directly, bypassing a subclass’s custom resolve_or_missing implementation. This is intentional for legacy resolve-only subclasses but may surprise users who overrode both methods with intertwined logic.

Context.resolve_or_missing now converts Undefined results from resolve into missing in legacy mode by checking isinstance(rv, Undefined). This requires Undefined to be imported or present in globals; any change to the Undefined import/name could break this path. Also, custom resolve methods that return Undefined-like objects not subclassing Undefined will no longer be translated to missing.

records.subject: Correctly use buffer for else frame in loops. Fixes #669

findings.message: Switched from dict.iteritems() to iteritems(local_overrides); this assumes iteritems is imported/defined (likely from jinja2._compat).
